summary: Independently certifies the Interactive Workflow + Publication CLI/Transport chapter (Phases 143A-145G.3V) as a coherent, secure, contract-compliant, restart-safe whole, without relying on any prior phase's own report or tests as authority. VERDICT: NOT CERTIFIED -- BLOCKING FINDINGS. Independent expectations were re-derived directly from IWC-001 v1.2, IWPC-001 v1.3, PEC-001 v1.1, and CHGR-001 v1.0 (full text reads), a chronological findings register was built from all phase reports 143A-145G.3V, and current production source was independently mapped (CLI parser/exit-code taxonomy, SessionApplicationService/PublicationApplicationService identity-check ordering, the SessionState transition table as coded, all three filesystem stores' atomicity/corruption/symlink handling, the PublicationCoordinator boundary, the composition root, and both existing AST-based forbidden-import tests) before any prior verdict was consulted. Live adversarial CLI execution against a disposable scratch repository found Blocking Finding H-1: a Confirmed decision session's readiness command, re-invoked after its first PublicationReadinessPackage has already been published, silently constructs and persists a second, independently publishable package (different package_id, same session), which governance-record publish then turns into a second, independent Canonical Human Governance Record for the same single Human Governance Act -- two CHGRs directly observed in the filesystem for one Confirmed session. Root cause: FilesystemPendingReadinessStore.find_by_session_id deliberately never returns a consumed/ record, the sole idempotency-by-key gate both ensure_readiness_package and persist_readiness_package rely on; no test anywhere exercises 'readiness again after publish'. The contractual uniqueness boundary was independently re-derived: no contract text permits this outcome (CHGR-001 SS2 defines a CHGR as representing 'one' Human Governance Act; IWPC-REQ-024's idempotency guarantee is unqualified; PEC-001's own replay guard is correctly scoped to package_id, the wrong key for this question). No phase report ever disclosed this as intentional; Phase 145G's own disclosed 'reports none not consumed' limitation mutated in consequence, unnoticed, once Phase 145G.1 wired real construction power into the same lookup. No repair was attempted -- the correct remedy (return the existing consumed package vs. raise a new domain error vs. some other resolution) is a design choice the contracts do not unambiguously dictate, outside this phase's narrow repair authority. Every other certified dimension held under independent adversarial scrutiny: chapter scope/ownership boundaries; cross-contract coherence; the ten-state machine's reachability and fail-closed terminal-state enforcement; CLI surface completeness; identity/authority/provenance separation (including fresh live re-confirmation of F-145G.2V-1's closure via wrong/missing/whitespace/case-variant identity adversarial testing); persistence atomicity/corruption/symlink/path-traversal handling (all independently attacked and held fail-closed); the Publication Execution boundary's structural integrity; dependency layering; documentation accuracy for the command surface; and full regression (chapter subset 1195/1195, fast_green 4391/4391, full governed suite 26654 passed/39 failed/10 skipped -- every failure independently traced to a cause outside this chapter). See docs/PHASE_145H_INTERACTIVE_WORKFLOW_CHAPTER_INDEPENDENT_CERTIFICATION.md.
